Title: March 12, 2026 - City of Boulder City Council Study Session
Overview: The council held a study session covering a Boulder Strong Day of Remembrance declaration, a preliminary look at forming a Downtown Development Authority (DDA) with tax increment financing and a possible November 2026 ballot, and a preliminary discussion of potential 2026 tax ballot measures. Council supported continued refinement of the DDA model with standalone governance and fiscal safeguards, and in the ballot discussion narrowed options to moving forward with the mid-range public realm mill levy, residential vacancy excise tax, general fund debt authorization, and combining dedicated sales taxes, while dropping the transformational and other mid-range options for 2026.

Topic1.Title: Boulder Strong Day of Remembrance Declaration
Topic1.Summary: Councilmember Wallach presented a declaration designating March 22 as the Boulder Day of Remembrance to honor the ten people killed in the 2021 King Soopers mass shooting. He read the victims' names and announced a remembrance ceremony at the Boulder Museum on March 22. The declaration was introduced as a ceremonial item before the work sessions began.

Topic2.Title: Downtown Development Authority Formation and Analysis
Topic2.Summary: Staff presented the proposed DDA as a tool to capture tax increment from property and sales tax growth within a study area and reinvest in downtown and the Hill. Staff's initial direction was a standalone DDA with a 1-2 year transition, a plan of development, and possible transfer of parking assets, with a June return to council and a possible November ballot. Council asked clarifying questions about voting thresholds, liability, base year, revenue sharing, and staff capacity. Most members supported continued refinement of the model, while Taisha Adams urged that climate and nature be included in the analysis.

Topic3.Title: Preliminary Discussion of 2026 Tax Ballot Measures
Topic3.Summary: Finance staff presented the long-term financial strategy, noting that 68% of city revenue is dedicated and sales tax is flattening. Staff reviewed transformational, mid-range, and structural ballot measure options and the timeline toward a May 14 narrowing and a June polling result. Council straw polls kept the mid-range public realm mill levy, residential vacancy excise tax, general fund debt authorization, and combining dedicated sales taxes for further work, and moved transformational options and the general mill levy off the 2026 list.
